title: SLA Ledger Proxy for deterministic residency & retention attestations
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a small authenticated proxy + ledger API that guarantees deterministic ingestion, ordering, and attestable delivery for all compliance-related events (residency assertions, retention policy changes, audit evidence). The proxy should offer SLA-backed acknowledgements, per-region residency markers, signed attestations for each committed event, and a durable export path for customers and audit teams.
goals: Deterministic sequence numbers for all compliance events committed during a time window
Produce signed attestations (timestamped) that can be served to auditors or retained alongside evidence exports
Expose an idempotent ingestion API and a webhook delivery contract with clear retry semantics and backpressure handling
Support region-anchored residency metadata and retention TTL enforcement metadata on each ledger row
Meet 99.9% API availability for committed deliveries in the first 30s, backed by SLO and monitoring
non_goals: Full multi-tenant archival ingestion pipeline (handled by separate archival service)
Replacing existing evidence storage systems — this is a transactional ledger and attestation layer only
api_contract_summary: POST /v1/compliance/ledger/events - idempotent ingestion. Required headers: Authorization, X-Redwood-Evidence-Id, X-Redwood-Region. Returns 202 + ledger_sequence or 409 on duplicate with existing sequence.
POST /v1/compliance/ledger/ack - acknowledges webhook delivery from external consumer; used to advance delivery window and permit safe TTL-based deletion.
GET  /v1/compliance/attestations/{sequence} - returns signed attestation (base64) and metadata for a ledger row.
GET  /v1/compliance/ledger/stream?from={seq}&region={r} - streaming cursor for internal replication and exports (kafka-backed).
design_decisions: Store ledger primary state in geo-partitioned CockroachDB to get strongly-ordered sequences per region while allowing global reads for exports
Use Kafka (dedicated topic per region) for high-throughput fan-out to downstream subscribers and archival exporters
Generate signed attestations as compact JSON Web Signatures (JWS) using customer-specific KMS key wrapping. Attestations persisted to S3 with lifecycle tied to retention policy
Expose only idempotency-key-based ingestion and assign internal sequence numbers to avoid relying on event timestamps for ordering

Make the proxy synchronous for acknowledgement (returns committed sequence) but perform attestation generation asynchronously with a <2s target; if attestation generation fails we mark the ledger row as pending and schedule retries
tradeoffs: CockroachDB gives strong consistency but higher write latency vs Dynamo append-only. We accept slightly higher p99 write latency to guarantee sequence correctness for audits
Asynchronous attestation generation reduces endpoint latency, but introduces a short window where a committed row has no attestation. We mitigate by marking state and instrumenting targeted alerts
Kafka introduces operational overhead (topics/partitions) versus an all-in-DB changefeed, but provides scalable fan-out to archive consumers and reduces coupling to DB schema
security_considerations: All ingress must be mTLS + token-based auth. Secondary attestations signed with KMS keys scoped per-tenant
Attestation artifacts in S3 encrypted with KMS and object-level immutability policy for configurable retention windows
Rate-limit ingestion per-tenant and provide circuit-breaker to avoid noisy tenants impacting the ledger
Audit logs for admin operations to modify ledger rows or force-replay must be immutable and stored in a separate retention-anchored bucket
acceptance_criteria: Can ingest 5k compliance events/sec (regional peak) with 99th percentile write latency < 120ms under load test
Each committed ledger row returns a deterministic increasing sequence number and can be fetched by sequence
Generate and serve signed attestations for 99% of committed rows within 2s; remaining rows retried until success
Webhook delivery contract documented and validated with at least two internal consumers; ack/negative-ack semantics proven in integration test
End-to-end integration test that simulates a region failover: events continue to be accepted and sequence gaps are reconciled after failback
implementation_notes: Schema: ledger(row_id UUID, seq_num INT8, tenant_id STRING, payload JSONB, region STRING, retention_ttl TIMESTAMP, attestation_status STRING, created_at TIMESTAMP)
Sequence allocation: use CockroachDB monotonic sequence per region via a small allocation table to avoid contention
Attestation worker: scalable K8s deployment reading kafka 'attestation-requests' topic and writing signed JWS to S3 with key format 'attestations/{tenant}/{sequence}.jws'
Webhook shipper: reuse existing event-shipper but add header validation and per-tenant retry backoffs; add capability to return canonical error codes for idempotent retries
Monitoring: add custom Prometheus metrics: ledger_commits_total, ledger_commit_latency_ms_bucket, attestation_pending_count, webhook_retry_rate
Dashboards: create Grafana dashboard link (placeholder) and a canary job that posts synthetic events every minute
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Initial PRD + technical spike completed. Chosen design: CockroachDB + Kafka + S3 attestations. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/SLA+Ledger+Proxy
2025-02-20: Prototype ingestion endpoint returning sequence numbers merged to feature branch. GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1267

2025-02-26: Load test (region eu-west-1 synthetic) reached 6k eps with p99 writes at 148ms; need further tuning on sequence allocation to reduce p99. Perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ledger-proxy
2025-03-01: Security design review scheduled; KMS keyscoping questions surfaced. Task created to harden attestation signing process
2025-03-04: Integration test harness for webhook acks implemented; observed duplicate-ack edge case requiring idempotency-prefix check
review_feedback: PM (Leah O'Connor): prefer explicit delivery SLA phrasing in API docs and a clear contract for customer-initiated replays
Design (Ravi Patel): request to add 'consistency' badge to exported attestation JSON and an example certificate format
Security (Marta Liu): require attestation replay protection and non-repudiation notes; recommend HSM-backed signing key rotation plan

Optimize sequence allocation codepath to get p99 write <120ms
